newsitem.title: BRAZIL: INTERVIEW-Real helped by increased loans.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Real helped by increased loans.

text.p: Brazil's Banco Real posted a 110 million real net profit in the first half of 1997, mostly due to a drop in loan defaults, higher credit operations and an increase in its client base, a bank executive said.

"Loan defaults fell, we increased loans and gained 850,000 clients in the first half," Rene Aduan, director general at Banco Real, told Reuters in a telephone interview to comment on the bank's earnings.

The bank's 1997 first half net consolidated profit fell when compared with the 236 million real net profit it posted a year ago. But Aduan noted Banco Real's 1996 first half net profit included 191 million reais in extraordinary revenues stemming from the sale of so-called FCVS debt paper.

Like other leading local retail banks, Banco Real, which is among Brazil's top 10 private banks, benefitted from lower defaults, which helped the bank cut expenses related to loan loss provisions made to cover bad debts. Such provisions totalled 279 million reais in the first semester.

Brazilian banks, especially in 1995, suffered from a surge in corporate and consumer defaults after the government introduced a policy of high interest rates and credit restrictions in the first phase of its already three-year-old Real anti-inflation plan.
High loan defaults led most banks to be cautious in the loan business, even after the government eased the credit limits and moved to gradually reduce interest rates.
"All banks are more selective," said Aduan.
Banco Real's total credit portfolio rose 35 percent to 7.198 billion reais in the first half from 5.331 billion reais in the same period a year ago, he said.
Aduan noted trade finance, particularly in the Mercosur region, contributed to the increase in the credit business.
Asset management growth also boosted Banco Real's first half results, he said. The bank manages 19.4 billion reais in assets, up 45 percent from 13.4 billion reais a year ago.
The bank closed the January-to-June period with total assets of 18.162 billion reais, up 28.4 percent from the same period a year ago.
With a net worth of 1.688 billion reais, the bank showed an annualized return on equity of 13.5 percent.

With a total client portfolio of 2.46 million customers, Banco Real has 1,757 outlets in Brazil and 37 branches in 13 other countries, Aduan said. He said the bank, which is present in all countries of the Mercosur region, plans to open branches in Venezuela, Peru and Ecuador next year.
It also plans to open a new branch in Bolivia. Banco Real already has one in La Paz, he added.
